title: No Cost to Correct
strengths: The relational schema, rendering view, and generated vacancy field align the disclosed artifact with the claimed record-world.
GOOD, normal wear, zero correction cost, dissent, and vacancy classification create genuine institutional pressure.
The database/WAL pair is formally irreducible and the unchanged main-file invariant is verified.
failures: HUD damage accounting and Census vacancy classification remain adjacent arguments rather than one causal mechanism.
The rectangle, pinholes, standing pile, and brass keyway are familiar traces whose language does not justify the apparatus burden.
Repeated GOOD and zero-cost fields make a thirty-one-line surface whose strongest contradiction occurs only at the end.
The WAL inserts the whole occupancy row, so presence and vacancy arrive together instead of an occupied unit being reclassified while nobody leaves.
revision_instruction: Preserve D001-D003 exactly. Subtract the HUD and domestic-trace branch. Build D004 with persons living and zero departures already in the base, one explicit usual-residence update in WAL, an AFTER UPDATE classification log, and an exhaustive every-table state contract.
comparison_limit: One internal later-turn cold review; not independent reader evidence.
non_claim: This internal review routes subtraction. It is not external uptake, admission, or evidence that D004 succeeds.
